subject: Next steps: POC plan & deployment mode recommendation

Hi Priya (and procurement team),

Great to speak earlier — appreciate you walking us through the HealthLynx integration goals and PHI constraints. Below is a short recap + a recommended POC approach to help you choose between Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private VPC/on-prem. I want to keep the first PoC low-friction while giving you a clear path to the more isolated options if needed.

Recap of needs we heard:
- Primary workload: real-time clinical note summarization and secure embeddings for search.
- Data sensitivity: some PHI elements; team needs evidence of encryption, audit logs, and controlled egress.
- Traffic profile: bursty daytime traffic, expected ~200 concurrent sessions at peak, median context length ~1k tokens.
- Success criteria: latency and quality thresholds, security signoffs.

Recommended phased POC (6 weeks total, flexible):
1) Week 0-1: Sandbox integration (Hosted API, isolated dev key)
   - Purpose: exercise SDK integration, end-to-end request flow, early quality checks against your prompt set.
   - Why Hosted first: fastest time-to-value and gives the team immediate telemetry (latency, token usage, model outputs).

2) Week 2-3: Parallel Dedicated sizing run (optional, recommended if you need predictable throughput or want to validate autoscaling)
   - Purpose: run Representative load (peak concurrency + 20%) on a Dedicated pool to measure 95p latency, token throughput, and cost profile.
   - When to pick Dedicated: if predictable latency under load and customer-managed isolation are priorities but PHI at-rest in our environment is acceptable under contract.

3) Week 4-6: Private evaluation (VPC or on-prem) if required
   - Purpose: run a short Private deployment trial (VPC peered or air-gapped on-prem) to validate KMS integration, audit logs, and SOC2 controls with live PHI data.
   - When to pick Private: when legal/regulatory requires no external-hosted PHI or you must bring all data behind your network.

Proposed PoC success criteria (measurable):
- Latency: 95th percentile generation latency < 120ms for short prompts (<256 tokens); < 300ms for 1k-token flows during normal load.
- Throughput: support sustained 200 concurrent sessions (approx 30 req/s) with autoscaling and <1% error rate.
- Quality: pass rate >= 85% on your prompt validation set for summarization fidelity (we can use the set you shared today).
- Security: encryption in transit and at rest, KMS integration validated, audit logs available and confirmable via our Console within 48 hours.
- Cost visibility: token-level cost breakdown available in Console; Dedicated run gives projected $/1M-token estimate.

Stakeholders we recommend loop in for the POC:
- HealthLynx: Priya (Product lead), Procurement contact (for trial terms), Security reviewer (for checklist items), Engineering lead (for integration).
- Redwood: Marissa (AE, owner), Rishi (SE, technical lead), Aditya (Sales manager, exec sponsor).

Attachments: HealthLynx_PoC_Scope.docx (detailed week-by-week plan). I also attached our Dedicated SLA and a Private VPC checklist for your security team to scan.

Ask: Can you confirm which of the following you want us to start with?
A) Hosted sandbox only (fastest)
B) Hosted sandbox + Dedicated sizing run (recommended path)
C) Fast-track Private trial (if legal requires PHI never touch hosted infra)

If B or C, can you share the security contact and procurement contact so we can draft a short trial agreement? If A, we can spin up a sandbox key and schedule a 45-minute kickoff this week.

Proposed next meeting windows: Thu 2/18 10:00-11:00 PST or Mon 2/22 9:00-10:00 PST.

Thanks — happy to adapt based on what you need.

Hi Priya — quick technical answers and an updated, concrete test plan you can share with security/procurement.

Regarding logs and PHI:
- Hosted sandbox: by default we do not persist request payloads to long-term logs. Short-term request traces (48–72h) are retained for debugging unless you ask us to enable persistent request logging. We also offer token-level redaction and a request-filtering webhook so you can strip PHI before it reaches Redwood. For a Hosted sandbox with any PHI, we recommend using de-identification + our request-filter.
- Dedicated/Private: Dedicated gives more isolated tenancy (your own GPU pool) with standard Redwood audit logs. Private VPC/on-prem puts the runtime inside your network — no customer data leaves your VPC unless you configure outbound routes.

Dedicated trial cost estimate:
- We can offer a 7-day Dedicated trial at a discounted evaluation rate; rough estimate for the sizing we discussed (equivalent of 2 x A100s sustained for sizing) is ~$3,500 for the week (this will be firmed up after workload profiling). I'll ask pricing to produce a one-line estimate for procurement.

Concrete technical POC tests (we recommend running these across Hosted sandbox + Dedicated sizing run in parallel where possible):
A) Latency/Throughput tests:
   - Target: 95p latency < 120ms for short prompts, sustained 30 req/s with concurrency emulated to 200 sessions.
   - Test: replay 1,000 representative requests over 10 minutes at increasing concurrency; measure cold-starts and steady-state.
B) KV cache + prefix caching:
   - Target: 80%+ cache hit rate for repeated context sequences to reduce per-token cost.
   - Test: run a mixed workload with repeated prefix sequences and measure effective token-per-response and cost delta.
C) Security validation:
   - Validate KMS integration: create test key and rotate; verify audit entries appear in Console within 24–48h.
   - Verify network controls for Dedicated (VPC peering) and run sample egress test.
D) Quality evaluation:
   - Run your prompt validation set (sample of 200 cases) and produce a simple pass/fail metric for fidelity, then review edge failures.

Attachments: I attached the Dedicated SLA and the Private VPC checklist for your security reviewer. I also put the proposed test harness in the shared Drive link Marissa included.

Next steps I can own:
- Share a one-line Dedicated trial estimate for procurement by EOD 2/16.
- Prep a short test harness (k6 + repro script) and a runbook for your eng team to execute the sizing run.

If you want, we can also redact/anonymize a subset of real examples with you to validate quality without hitting PHI concerns early.
